about.title: About the data
about.intro: Smog Radar answers two everyday questions, whether to go for a walk and whether to open the windows, from an air quality forecast. Here is where the numbers come from and how the answers are made.
about.sourceText: Air quality comes from the {openMeteo}, which serves the {cams} European air quality forecast: hourly values on a grid of roughly 11 km. Place search uses Open-Meteo's geocoding.
about.modelNote: {strong} A busy street or a neighbour's chimney can make the air on your doorstep worse than the number here. Smog Radar is general information, not medical advice.
about.modelNoteStrong: These are modelled values, not station measurements.
about.eaqiText: The index used across the EU. Each pollutant (PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, O₃) gets its own sub-index; the overall AQI is the highest of them, which is why the page names the pollutant that “sets the index”.
about.walkBasis: Follows the European Environment Agency's health advice for each AQI band: most people are advised to cut down intense outdoor activity from “poor”, sensitive people from “moderate”.
about.windowsBasis: The EEA gives no advice on ventilation, so this rule is ours. Rooms still need fresh air, so the middle answer is a short airing rather than keeping the windows shut.
about.betterText: When an answer isn't the best one, Smog Radar looks ahead for the first hour that would be, and highlights the cleanest {hours} hours on the chart. Both only consider {from} to {to} local time; nobody wants a walk suggestion for 3 a.m.
about.whoText: For context, each pollutant is compared with the {who}. Those are 24-hour (or 8-hour) averages and our values are hourly, so the comparison is a pointer, not a compliance check. The answers themselves use the European AQI only.
about.privacyText: No accounts, no analytics, no tracking. “Use my location” asks your browser once; the position is rounded to about 1 km before it leaves your browser, and the rounded position is used only to fetch the forecast from Open-Meteo. Cookies remember your last place, your language and whether sensitive mode is on, so the page opens where you left it.
